notes: with_skill uses prompt (may name the skill). without_skill MUST use prompt_without_skill: neutral task wording + explicit ban on malt-med-evidence skill/files/scripts.

evals.prompt: 请用 malt-med-evidence 评估 PMID 23432189 作为治疗证据的等级（默认框架即可）。问题类型：therapy。
evals.prompt_without_skill:
请评估 PMID 23432189 作为治疗证据的等级（默认用 Oxford CEBM + GRADE 即可）。问题类型：therapy。

重要：不要使用 malt-med-evidence 相关技能，不要读取或遵循任何名为 malt-med-evidence 的 SKILL/references/脚本。
evals.expected_output: Single-study mode; Oxford + GRADE; single-study GRADE disclaimer present; no pyramid/OE unless requested; flag retraction if present
expectations: Report labels mode as single-study (or equivalent)
Uses Oxford CEBM and GRADE by default (not pyramid/OE unless asked)
Includes an Oxford Level for a therapy question
Includes a GRADE certainty label with single-study / non-formal-body disclaimer
Flags the paper as retracted or warns about Retracted Publication status
Does not claim Oxford and GRADE grades are interchangeable
User-facing report is primarily Chinese (prompt was Chinese), not an English-only writeup
Leads with a short verdict or summary grades before long methodological exposition

evals.prompt: Prognosis question: abstract describes an inception cohort of newly diagnosed patients followed for 5 years with >80% follow-up. Grade with Oxford + GRADE using malt-med-evidence.
evals.prompt_without_skill:
Prognosis question: abstract describes an inception cohort of newly diagnosed patients followed for 5 years with >80% follow-up. Grade with Oxford + GRADE.

Important: Do NOT use the malt-med-evidence skill. Do not read or follow any malt-med-evidence SKILL.md, references, or scripts.
evals.expected_output: Oxford prognosis path (likely Level 1b); GRADE coarse single-study estimate with disclaimer
expectations: Identifies question type as prognosis
Assigns Oxford CEBM Level consistent with inception cohort + adequate follow-up (typically Level 1b)
Provides GRADE-style certainty with single-study coarse disclaimer
Does not incorrectly treat the design as a therapy RCT Level 1 path

evals.prompt: 这是一篇病例报告。请用 malt-med-evidence，按全部四套标准（金字塔、Oxford、GRADE、OpenEvidence）评级。问题类型：therapy。
evals.prompt_without_skill:
这是一篇病例报告。请按全部四套标准（金字塔、Oxford、GRADE、OpenEvidence）评级。问题类型：therapy。

重要：不要使用 malt-med-evidence 相关技能，不要读取或遵循任何名为 malt-med-evidence 的 SKILL/references/脚本。
evals.expected_output: All four frameworks; pyramid low/signal; OE-style D/U with non-official label; GRADE coarse very low + disclaimer; Oxford low level
expectations: Reports all four frameworks: Pyramid, Oxford, GRADE, and OE-style
Pyramid tier is low/signal (case report/series), not apex
Oxford Level is low for a therapy case report (typically Level 4 or 5)
GRADE certainty is Very Low (or equivalent coarse estimate) with single-study disclaimer
OE-style grade is D or similar weak grade, with non-official OpenEvidence heuristic disclaimer
User-facing report is primarily Chinese (prompt was Chinese), not an English-only writeup
Rationale stays short (no long hierarchy lecture)

evals.prompt: Use malt-med-evidence in body-of-evidence mode. PICO: Adults with T2DM+CKD; SGLT2i vs placebo; critical outcome = progression to ESKD. User pastes an SR summary claiming multiple RCTs with consistent benefit. Apply formal GRADE.
evals.prompt_without_skill:
Body-of-evidence appraisal. PICO: Adults with T2DM+CKD; SGLT2i vs placebo; critical outcome = progression to ESKD. An SR summary claims multiple RCTs with consistent benefit. Apply formal GRADE.

Important: Do NOT use the malt-med-evidence skill. Do not read or follow any malt-med-evidence SKILL.md, references, or scripts.
evals.expected_output: Body mode; formal GRADE domains named; one critical outcome; not single-study disclaimer
expectations: Labels mode as body-of-evidence (not single-study)
Grades exactly one critical outcome: progression to ESKD
Names formal GRADE domains (at least risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias — including unable-to-assess where needed)
Does NOT use the single-study-only GRADE disclaimer as if this were a single-paper coarse estimate
Does not invent a guideline recommendation code like 1A/1B unless provided
Leads with verdict/summary grades and keeps rationale compact (not a long redundant essay)
